step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Philosopher Frank Ramsey, who died in 1930 aged 26

step5_concept_grounding: Retrospective speculative discussion of Weil's disease (leptospirosis) as an unverified historical hypothesis for death in 1930

evidence_items.source_quote: In mid-November 1929 Ramsey developed an acute febrile illness after a College feast (a formal occasion involving many courses of rich food, washed down with much alcohol).

rationale: A historical biographical case report exploring speculative retrospective causes of death for philosopher Frank Ramsey, who died in 1930. The final contemporaneous death certificate recorded cholangitis and hepatitis. Leptospirosis (Weil's disease) is mentioned solely as a modern retrospective hypothesis in the abstract and discussion, without clinical or diagnostic verification in the patient during life. Excluded as non-target case.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 46-year-old male paddy field worker presenting with acute febrile illness, initially suspected of leptospirosis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as provisional working diagnosis and ruled out by negative paired ELISA

evidence_items.source_quote: An ELISA test done for IgM and IgG against leptospira on day 7 and repeated on day 18 delivered negative results.
evidence_items.test_name: ELISA for leptospira IgM and IgG

rationale: A 46-year-old rice paddy worker presented with fever, acute kidney injury, and pulmonary edema. Leptospirosis was suspected as the provisional diagnosis, but paired ELISA testing for Leptospira IgM and IgG on days 7 and 18 was negative, while hantavirus IgM was confirmed positive. Target disease was explicitly tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 57-year-old male with acute febrile illness, oliguria, and pulmonary edema evaluated for Weil's disease

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as working diagnosis and ruled out by negative MAT

evidence_items.source_quote: Blood was taken for a microscopic agglutination test (MAT) for IgM and IgG against leptospira on day 10 and was also negative.

rationale: A 57-year-old male presented with fever, myalgias, oliguria, and pulmonary edema with a working diagnosis of Weil's disease. Blood taken on day 10 for MAT (IgM and IgG) was negative, whereas hantavirus IgM serology was positive. Leptospirosis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 42-year-old male presenting with fever, confusion, and left arm weakness post-scuba diving in a quarry

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis considered in differential diagnosis for acute post-diving infection and screened negative

evidence_items.source_quote: He was admitted and treated for an ischaemic stroke and meningitis with empirical antibiotics. A magnetic resonance scan (MRI) was conducted followed by vasculitis screen.

rationale: A 42-year-old male developed fever, confusion, and neurological deficits after diving in a freshwater quarry. He was investigated for meningitis and systemic infection; leptospirosis and vasculitis screening were both negative. Decompression illness secondary to patent foramen ovale was confirmed as the diagnosis. Target disease was screened and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old male presenting with fever, jaundice, and AKI, initially suspected of leptospirosis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as working diagnosis and ruled out by negative antibody and PCR assays

evidence_items.source_quote: Later on, antibody and PCR assays for Leptospira were negative. F. necrophorum was isolated in blood cultures on the second day.
evidence_items.test_name: Antibody and PCR assays for Leptospira

rationale: A 38-year-old male presented with fever, severe jaundice, and anuric AKI mimicking Weil's disease. Specific Leptospira antibody and PCR assays were negative, while blood cultures confirmed Fusobacterium necrophorum bacteremia. Target disease was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old male presenting with acute febrile illness, arthralgia, and myalgia evaluated for leptospirosis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as endemic differential and tested negative by IgM and IgG serology

evidence_items.source_quote: leptospira IgM and IgG performed on day 7 were negative.

rationale: A 30-year-old male presented with acute febrile illness and multiorgan involvement. Leptospira IgM and IgG performed on day 7 were negative, whereas hantavirus IgM was repeatedly positive. Target disease was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 37-year-old male farmer presenting with fever, ARDS, and respiratory failure

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as endemic differential and tested negative by IgM serology

evidence_items.source_quote: Dengue IgM and leptospirosis IgM done on day 6 illness were negative.

rationale: A 37-year-old farmer presented with fever, dyspnea, and ARDS. Leptospirosis IgM serology on day 6 was negative, and hantavirus IgM was positive on days 3 and 25. Target disease was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 33-year-old male presenting with acute oxidative hemolysis and AKI due to G6PD deficiency after herbal remedy

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated in acute hepatonephritis and ruled out by negative PCR and paired MAT

evidence_items.source_quote: Leptospiral polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was negative and paired leptospiral microscopic agglutination test (MAT) did not demonstrate a fourfold rise and neither of the titers were significant.

rationale: A 33-year-old male developed dark urine, jaundice, and anuric AKI following ingestion of an Acalypha herbal remedy. Leptospirosis was evaluated and excluded with negative PCR and paired MAT showing no significant titers, while acute G6PD-mediated oxidative hemolysis was confirmed. Target disease ruled out -> NEGATIVE.
